note: Editorial file. 'now' must be factual and sourced; 'meaning' is Procurement Signal's analysis. Refresh each newsroom run when the cost monitor or category news changes. 'leverage' (1 = suppliers hold it, 5 = procurement holds it), 'risk', 'riskWhy', 'move' and 'when' are Procurement Signal's assessment, built from the cited sources.

steel.now: Producer prices hit a new high in August, up 23.4% on the year. Importers also pay a 50% Section 232 duty on full customs value since April 6.
steel.meaning: Landed cost for imported steel is rising faster than the index shows. Suppliers have pricing power, so flat annual increases will lag the market.
steel.riskWhy: ISM respondents report several steel grades in short supply, and AI and data center demand is stretching domestic mill capacity. Imports carry a 50% duty on full value.
steel.move: Lock supply on critical grades with domestic mills and index the rest to a published steel price.
steel.label: Steel

aluminum.now: Prices are 5.9% below their June high but still 27.3% above a year ago. Imports carry a 50% Section 232 duty on full value.
aluminum.meaning: Contracts priced at spring highs are now above market. The pullback is a window to re-quote, but the duty keeps imported landed cost elevated.
aluminum.riskWhy: Prices are below the June high, but the 50% Section 232 duty keeps imported landed cost high and ISM still lists aluminum as rising.
aluminum.move: Re-quote contracts priced at the spring peak and ask for index-linked terms going forward.
aluminum.when: Now, while prices sit below the June high
aluminum.label: Aluminum

copper.now: Copper and brass mill shapes are at a 12-month high, up 20.9% on the year, and semi-finished copper carries a 50% Section 232 duty. Refined cathode is still exempt: a proposed 15% tariff from Jan. 1, 2027 has not been decided, U.S. stocks are about 1.6 million tons (Macquarie) and the COMEX premium over LME has fallen almost 90% from its 2025 peak.
copper.meaning: Domestic metal is plentiful and the U.S. premium is shrinking, so 2027 price letters should not pre-load a refined-copper tariff. Expect pass-through on semi-finished copper, but push for COMEX-linked prices to follow the narrowing premium.

sources.name: Procurement Signal: U.S. copper stocks and the pending refined-copper tariff
ScrapMonster — U.S. copper stockpile hits 1.6M tons

copper.riskWhy: A refined-copper tariff decision could come at any time and would widen U.S. premiums again; semi-finished copper already pays 50% under Section 232.
copper.move: Reject pre-loaded tariff increases, split metal from conversion cost and agree a tariff trigger clause now.
copper.when: Before 2027 price letters and any Jan. 1 tariff decision
copper.label: Copper and brass

resins.now: Plastic resin prices have fallen 8.5% over three months and are among the categories that turned lower this year.
resins.meaning: Input costs for packaging and molded-part suppliers are falling. Category managers have leverage to re-quote rather than accept increases set earlier in the year.
resins.riskWhy: Producer prices fell 8.5% over three months through August, and BLS listed thermoplastic resins among the items that declined in September, although ISM respondents reported resin prices rising.
resins.move: Re-bid packaging and molded parts, and ask for decreases tied to a resin index.
resins.label: Plastic resins

chemicals.now: Industrial chemical prices have eased over three months but remain 13.3% above a year ago.
chemicals.meaning: The market has turned in procurement's favor. Before accepting increases, ask suppliers to show how lower input costs are reflected in their price.

sources.name: Procurement Signal: six months into the U.S.–Iran war

chemicals.riskWhy: Prices have eased over three months, but petroleum-based feedstocks remain exposed to the war with Iran and Strait of Hormuz disruption.
chemicals.move: Ask suppliers to show how lower input costs are reflected before accepting any increase.
chemicals.label: Industrial chemicals

diesel.now: Producer prices for diesel fuel rose 21.0% in September at the intermediate stage, after a 17.7% jump in August. The IEA says diesel hit records near $220 a barrel in September and the market will stay tight well into 2027, with stocks unlikely to rebuild before the second half of 2027.
diesel.meaning: Plan for a long plateau, not a winter spike. Fuel surcharge tables in carrier and supplier contracts will matter for the whole 2027 contract term, and indexed fuel passes any relief back faster than fixed all-in rates.

sources.name: Procurement Signal: IEA sees diesel tight into 2027
Procurement Signal: diesel at a record and fuel surcharges
Procurement Signal: six months into the U.S.–Iran war

diesel.riskWhy: The IEA expects gasoil to stay tight well into 2027 and calls the Gulf supply recovery fragile; Houthi strikes hit Aramco's Dhahran headquarters on Oct. 13.
diesel.move: Keep fuel separate from linehaul in 2027 awards and tie every surcharge to the weekly DOE/EIA diesel index.
diesel.label: Diesel fuel

ocean.now: Deep-sea freight is up 32.0% on the year. Trans-Pacific spot rates hold above $8,000 per FEU to the West Coast while Asia–Europe rates have fallen 34% since July, and only 27% of vessels arrive on schedule.
ocean.meaning: Treat ocean as two markets. Push for lower long-term rates on Asia–Europe; on the trans-Pacific, use shorter terms or index-linked pricing and buffer lead times for six-day average delays.

sources.name: Procurement Signal: ocean rates split by trade lane
Procurement Signal: Port of Los Angeles record September

ocean.riskWhy: Only 27% of vessels arrive on schedule, with delays averaging six days. Trans-Pacific rates are high while Asia–Europe rates have fallen 34% since July.
ocean.move: Lock lower long-term rates on Asia–Europe and keep trans-Pacific terms short or index-linked.
ocean.label: Ocean freight

trucking.now: Transportation and warehousing producer prices rose 3.4% in September, and BLS cited higher truck freight prices. Contract truckload rates hit a 52-week high in October as carriers exit the market faster than freight volumes fall.
trucking.meaning: The official index lags the market. Expect 2027 freight bids to price higher; protect routing-guide compliance with realistic rates and shorter award terms on volatile lanes.

sources.name: Procurement Signal: truckload contract rates at a 52-week high

trucking.riskWhy: Carriers are leaving the market faster than freight is falling, tender rejections are near 14% and broker consolidation is reducing options.
trucking.move: Segment lanes, commit volume on core lanes and pay for capacity where service matters.
trucking.label: Truckload freight

semis.now: Semiconductors are the only tracked category below year-ago prices, down 3.1%. Section 232 tariffs on semiconductors are in effect.
semis.meaning: Supplier prices are softening even as duties apply to imports. Compare landed cost, not just quoted price, before renegotiating.

sources.name: Procurement Signal: China rare earth export pause ends Nov. 10

semis.riskWhy: The producer price index is down, but memory chips are on allocation as AI data centers absorb supply. ISM lists memory, circuit boards and electronic components as short. China's suspension of wider rare earth and battery-material export controls ends Nov. 10 unless extended.
semis.move: Treat memory separately: secure allocation and extend forecasts, then re-quote other components.
semis.label: Semiconductors and memory

electrical.now: Electrical machinery and equipment prices are up 13.5% on the year. Some metal-intensive grid equipment carries a 15% Section 232 rate through 2027.
electrical.meaning: Metal costs and duties are both feeding into equipment pricing. Budget for landed cost above the index for imported electrical equipment.

sources.name: Procurement Signal: October factory investments, incl. transformer steel
Procurement Signal: China rare earth export pause ends Nov. 10

electrical.riskWhy: ISM respondents report electrical components in short supply, and capital equipment lead times average 176 days. Some grid equipment carries a 15% Section 232 rate. China's pause on wider rare earth export controls, which cover magnets used in motors, ends Nov. 10 unless extended.
electrical.move: Order long-lead equipment early, fix price at order and qualify a second source for critical parts.
electrical.label: Electrical equipment

lumber.now: Lumber prices are up 7.6% on the year, and Section 232 tariffs on wood products are in effect.
lumber.meaning: Pallet and crating costs follow lumber. Check how pallet and packaging suppliers price wood content in their contracts.

sources.name: Procurement Signal: wood and furniture tariffs

lumber.riskWhy: Section 232 duties on wood are in effect, and cabinet, vanity and upholstered furniture rates rise on Jan. 1. EU deforestation rules start Dec. 30 for wood products.
lumber.move: Check how pallet, crating and furniture suppliers price wood content and duty, and confirm country of origin.
lumber.label: Lumber and wood

paper.now: Converted paper and paperboard, including corrugated boxes, is up 4.4% on the year but accelerating to a 12.9% annualized pace.
paper.meaning: Box pricing is turning up from a low base. Check when corrugated contracts reset before increases arrive.
paper.riskWhy: Supply is available, but corrugated and paperboard prices are turning up from a low base at a 12.9% annualized pace.
paper.move: Lock corrugated pricing before contracts reset and tie future changes to a published index.
paper.label: Corrugated and paperboard
